coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No mandatory household-employer register or filing found. Duty sits on recruitment agencies: ILO (28 Nov 2025) says 116 private employment agencies are registered, licences harmonised to one year, digital monitoring being explored (mainly Zanzibar). Pool too small; see candidate on agencies. Household employer payroll falls under K07/K14 (rejected).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No enacted licensing regime found for Mainland. Only an African Review item (undated) quoting the Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade on a proposed law to supervise the scrap trade. Watch item. Other results were Trinidad/Kenya.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; the combined used-parts search surfaced no dealer or pawnbroker register. Pawnbroking is not clearly regulated under a dedicated law (unverified).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Only the 20% set-aside / BoT gold purchase programme (Oct 2024), i.e. K05. Jewellery-buyer licensing rules not found.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or parts-dealer register found. New TBS pre-shipment (PVoC) inspection for used spare parts: Japan from 1 Jan 2026, UAE from 21 Jun 2026, UK from 26 Jun 2026, 15% penalty on uninspected goods. Used tyres banned. See candidate.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Livestock Identification, Registration and Traceability Act 2010 (Mainland only); RFID ear tags, very low uptake; Meat Industry Act 2006 provides registration of livestock traders and market operators; TMX online livestock auction planned. Movement permit and levy details not found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Meat Industry Act 2006 (Tanzania Meat Board). Livestock Minister directive, dated 28 Jul 2026, to close butchers and slaughterhouses operating in unregistered premises. TMB retention fee TZS 100,000 per year (CTI page, 2023). No portal or forms named. See candidate.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Beekeeping Act 2002 and General Regulations 2005 (licences/permits). Government Digital Traceability System for honey and a national honey trademark (Oct 2024) already exist. Honey produced 33,861 t in 2024. State system covers the need; weak.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinary Act 2003: vets, paraprofessionals and veterinary practice facilities must register with the Veterinary Council of Tanzania; TFDA/TMDA overlap by MoU. No 2025 portal, fee or deadline found.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K06. Water Resources Management Act 2009 amended 2022 (Act 8); WUMIS online permit system already live in all nine basin boards (2022 report), which weakens K06. Private Boreholes Services Rules 2013 (TZS 100,000 per borehole registration) cover borehole suppliers in licensed areas.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Hazardous Waste Control and Management Regulations 2021 and Environment Act s.133 (permit to transport hazardous waste; NEMC registration for hazardous waste traders). No rule found for septic/exhauster operators. Thin.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: OSHA Act 2003; OSH (Lifting Appliances and Gears) Rules 2015; OSH (Vessels under Pressure) Regulations 2016; older fee rules require inspection providers to be registered annually with the Chief Inspector. Examination frequency and OSHA portal not confirmed.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water Supply and Sanitation Act 2019 (community organisations registered and monitored by RUWASA; water authorities need an EWURA licence, class I-III; Water Supply Regulations 2019 GN 828; Licensing and Quality of Service Rules 2020 GN 849). Buyers are community committees with low ability to pay; reporting duties unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Plant Health Regulations 2023 (GN 284) license pesticide dealers. TPHPA withdrew 805 pesticides and banned their import on 22 Jan 2026 (130 dangerous active ingredients, 675 lapsed registrations), with up to 2 years to exhaust stock under supervision. A search summary mentions inspection of about 50,000 pesticide shops in 2025/26 (unverified). Fertiliser dealers (TFRA) not searched.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: 116 registered private employment agencies (ILO, Nov 2025); one-year licences; review of registration, licensing and inspection systems under way; overseas recruitment must go via TaESA. Pool is small.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Only Ministry of Health mortuary guidelines (2020, 2022 version) covering hospital and stand-alone mortuaries and funeral homes, plus Graves (Removal) Regulations 1970. No licensing or periodic-return duty found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NGO Act 2002 with 2018/2019 regulations (Mainland): NGOs receiving over TZS 20m must publish funding sources and spending twice a year; funding contracts to the Registrar within 14 days; NGO renewal regulations 2019. Zanzibar has a separate NGO Registrar. Halal supervision not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: LATRA licenses daladala routes (new routes need new 15-20 seat vehicles; temporary permits for 150 buses on Morogoro Road Nov 2025; renewal barred on the BRT corridor). Bajaji and bodaboda are not licensed as public transport. LATRA and TRA e-ticketing for daladalas planned (undated). Driver verification ran in 2023.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Bureau de change: Foreign Exchange (Bureau de Change) Regulations 2023 (GN 730, in force 6 Oct 2023): classes A/B/C, Class B capital TZS 200m and 100% local ownership, AML, e-fiscal receipts, regular reports to BoT. TRA August 2025 one-month grace for unregistered online/home-based sellers (TIN, EFD receipts). IDRAS live from 9 Feb 2026. No machinga ID source found.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: Motor Vehicle Driving Schools (Licensing) Act, 12-month licence, police oversight, 161 schools deregistered (undated). Day care: Day Care Centres Act repealed 2010, Law of the Child Act plus 2020 ministry guidelines. Food producers: TMDA food premises scheme not confirmed (search returned nothing relevant). Tattoo studios not found. Hunting outfitters covered by K02.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: EWURA licenses retail outlets (2,597 outlets as of June 2024 per an April 2025 energy report; Oct 2025 warning about building stations without construction permits; notice that suburban stations must sign supply contracts; monthly cap prices must be displayed). No evidence found of a monthly retailer return; LPG distributors not searched. Mainland only (Zanzibar has ZURA/ZPRA, not checked). Candidate C09 logged as unverified.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Warehouse Receipts Act Cap 339 R.E. 2023 and WR Regulations GN 109/2016; regulator WRRB (successor to TWLB), 23 regions, 18 commodities, TMX trading. Cashew buyers need a CBT licence and an online TMX buyer declaration per season (only about 47 licensed firms in one year). COPRA contract-farming regulations (GN 158H, 30 Jun 2026) are the new item (C01). Tobacco and coffee buyer licences not found. Mainland only.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: SACCOS are registered under the Co-operative Societies Act and supervised by BoT as Tier 3 microfinance providers (Microfinance (SACCOS) Regulations 2019). Software already sold: Kalen SAMIS, MicrofinPro, UBX, Amala; Mixx/UBX/SCCULT payments partnership. No specific BoT report format found. Candidate C03 (weak). Mainland only; Zanzibar SACCOS rules not checked.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: NHIF claims is already K04/K09. New item: Private Health Laboratories Board registration (Act Cap 286) plus HFRS online registration/renewal for facilities via GePG; Miscellaneous Laws (Amendments) Bill 2026, tabled 1 Sep 2026, would raise penalties for unregistered labs and widen lab categories. Candidate C05.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: GCLA Customer Chemicals Management Portal (CCMP): dealers must register, hold permits/certificates and file precursor-chemical returns online; Nov 2024 GCLA told big suppliers to stop selling to unregistered small dealers; June 2026 stress on supply-chain control. State portal exists. Candidate C04. ADDO/pharmacy: no 2025 electronic registration found; 2019 ADDO regulations (GN 185) only; nothing new beyond K17.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Two searches. No governing statute or regulator confirmed. Found: TBS voluntary code for manned guarding, TSIA industry body plan for member certification, March 2026 report on regulated guard wages and untrained guards. Candidate C06 marked unverified. Cleaning and manpower agencies not found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: CRB registration (Contractors Registration Act Cap 235, five classes, deregistration after two years of unpaid annual fees, BRELA prerequisite); ERB annual renewal via MIS portal by 31 March (engineers, not contractors). NCC local-content returns not found. Mining local content is K01 and dealer returns K05. Nothing new beyond K01/K05; C10 weak.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: No enacted real estate regulator: a Real Estate Regulatory Authority bill was reported as nearing Cabinet (Citizen; law-firm guide dated 2026), covering brokers and agents, so a licensing wave may follow. FIU DNFBP AML/CFT guide (Jan 2023) puts DNFBPs under STR duties after 2022 amendments; no goAML onboarding notice found. Candidates C07 and C08.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Hotels Act has a guest register and a hotels levy; Tourism Act 2008 and Tourism Accommodation Facilities Regulations (Amendment) 2019 require visitors to be registered on the ministry portal, reportedly for registered tourist facilities and not guest houses (unclear). Zanzibar PMS compliance is K10/K16 (rejected). Candidate C11 weak.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Timber: Export of Timber Act Cap 274; TFS import permit TZS 115,000 per m3 (third-party listing); EUDR vendor TraceX targets Tanzanian wood exporters. No TFS e-permit or transit-pass evidence found. Coffee EUDR is K11 and fish is K13 (rejected). New: COPRA contract-farming registry (C01) and avocado buyer registry plan.

coverage.category: 31. Contract farming registry (COPRA, non-board crops)
coverage.found: Food Security (Contract Farming) Regulations, GN 158H, 30 Jun 2026: written contracts registered digitally with COPRA before planting (area, projected yield, named buyer); fines TZS 1-5m for individuals, at least TZS 2m for corporates. Source is news only; primary gazette not read. C01.

coverage.category: 32. Non-deposit-taking microfinance providers (BoT Microfinance Regulations 2025)
coverage.found: Clyde & Co April 2025 summary of the draft Microfinance Regulations 2025: minimum capital TZS 20m (local) or TZS 500m (foreign-owned), liquidity 1% of gross loans, prior BoT approval for CEO and governors, may now act as mobile money agents. Article said still draft; reporting schedule not described. C02.

coverage.category: 33. OSHA, Fire and Rescue and WCF workplace compliance for small premises
coverage.found: OSHA workplace registration plus a 12-month compliance licence (OHS Act ss 16-17; fines TZS 1-5m or up to 12 months' jail); Fire safety certificate under Fire and Rescue Act 2008 (GN 106/2008) via portal.zimamoto.go.tz; WCF registration. Annual fire renewal and fees unconfirmed. C12.

coverage.category: 34. Foreign exchange bureaux and mobile money agency (BoT)
coverage.found: Foreign Exchange (Bureau de Change) Regulations 2023 in force 6 Oct 2023: Classes A, B, C (C hotels only); ownership change notice within 7 days, name change within 14 days; an undated report says capital was raised (Class A to TZS 300m, Class B to TZS 1bn). Periodic returns not found. C13 weak (small buyer pool).

coverage.category: 35. Crop board buyer licensing (cashew, avocado, other)
coverage.found: Cashewnut Industry Act 2009: buyers licensed by CBT per season, online buyer declaration on TMX, export permit per lot. Avocado buyer registry planned by COPRA. Tobacco and coffee not found. C14 weak.

coverage.category: 36. Private security guard firms (country-specific licensing)
coverage.found: See category 26 and C06; statute and regulator not identified in two searches.

coverage.category: 37. Chemical dealers under GCLA (country-specific)
coverage.found: Covered under category 25 and C04.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Mainland: pawnbroking is prohibited outright under the Pawnbroking (Prohibition) Act, Cap. 175 (1965, consolidated 2002/2019), so there is no pawnbroker licence or register to build on. The Pawnbrokers Ordinance (Cap. 226) was repealed. Source: tanzlii.org/en/akn/tz/act/1965/17/eng@2002-07-31 (search snippet only; the WebFetch got HTTP 403). Not checked: Zanzibar pawn rules, and any amendments after 2019. No statutory second-hand dealer register or police dealer-book regime turned up for general goods, phones or used cars; the only phone-related controls are TCRA IMEI blocking (CEIR) and police/TCRA meetings with phone vendors (Dodoma, 2025). Used clothing (mitumba): TBS notice of 2 Jul 2025 on banned items under TZS 758:2023/EAS 356:2019, with no dealer register. Used cars: TRA transfer and registration with a dealer tax invoice, plus TBS pre-shipment inspection extended to the UK and UAE (notices of May 2026). Duties fall on importers or vehicle owners, with no dealer-premises register found. Used electronics: TCRA importer licence, type approval, eco-levy via GePG since May 2023, and E-waste Regulations 2021 (sale, refurbishing and dismantling in scope). The burden falls mainly on importers and distributors, and a retail or refurbisher licence was not confirmed. Informal collateral lending: the Microfinance Act 2018 Tier 4 covers individual moneylenders and community groups, which must register with BoT or a delegated authority or local government. This is a lender category, not second-hand dealing, so it likely belongs to the savings-group or co-operative worker (category 23). Nothing new beyond K03 and K17 for this category.
